subtopics.title: UAE Visit: Strategic Outcomes
subtopics.summary: PM Modi's UAE visit produced agreements and proposals on energy security, LPG supply, shipbuilding and defence, and AI infrastructure. The energy outcomes centre on strategic crude storage and an LPG supply partnership with ADNOC. Investment interest in India's infrastructure sector was also noted.
facts: MoU between Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Limited and Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) for strategic collaboration.
Proposal to store up to 30 million barrels of ADNOC crude oil in India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves.
Discussions on storing crude oil in Fujairah under India's Overseas Strategic Reserve Framework.
IOCL and ADNOC signed a strategic collaboration agreement on LPG supply security; a long-term LPG sale deal between ADNOC Gas and IOCL is a potential deal.
Framework advanced for a Strategic Defence Partnership between India and the UAE.
Cochin Shipyard and Drydocks World MoU to establish a Ship Repair Cluster at Vadinar.
Cooperation includes offshore fabrication under the Maritime Development Fund Scheme.
Term sheet signed for setting up 8 Exaflop Super Computing Clusters.
Partnership between C-DAC and G42 under India's AI Mission.
Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and National Infrastructure and Investment Fund to explore investments up to US$1 billion in India's infrastructure sector.

subtopics.title: UAE: Trade, Diaspora and Country Profile
subtopics.summary: India-UAE trade in FY 2025-26 stood at US$100 billion, and the UAE is among India's largest energy suppliers and export destinations. The 2022 CEPA and the UAE's share of India's remittance flows are key economic links. The booklet also profiles the UAE's government and the Kafala sponsorship system.
facts: Trade between India and the UAE in FY 2025-26: US$100 billion.
UAE is India's 2nd largest export destination, after the US.
UAE is India's 3rd largest crude oil source.
UAE is India's 3rd largest supplier of LNG and 2nd largest supplier of LPG.
UAE is the only nation participating in India's Strategic Reserve Programme.
In 2022, India was the first country with which the UAE signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
UAE accounted for 18% of India's remittance flows.
UAE is a federal, elective monarchy of 7 emirates; capital Abu Dhabi; currency dirham.
Kafala system: a sponsorship system in Gulf countries that ties a foreign worker's visa and legal status to an in-country sponsor, typically the employer.
Indian nationals form the largest expatriate community within the UAE.

subtopics.title: Norway, Nordic Group and Sweden
subtopics.summary: PM Modi made the first bilateral visit by an Indian PM to Norway in 43 years and attended the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in Oslo. Ties with Norway were upgraded to a Green Strategic Partnership, and ties with Sweden were elevated to a Strategic Partnership. The core Nordic group has five countries.
facts: PM Modi undertook the first bilateral visit by an Indian PM to Norway in 43 years.
The 3rd India-Nordic Summit was held in Oslo; earlier summits were in Stockholm (2018) and Copenhagen (2022).
India and Norway upgraded ties to a Green Strategic Partnership covering clean energy transition, climate resilience, blue economy and green shipping.
Norway formally joined India's Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative.
PM Modi was awarded Norway's highest civilian honour, the Grand Cross of the Royal Norwegian Order of Merit.
India-EFTA TEPA was signed in 2024.
Norwegian Sovereign Wealth Fund (GPFG) has invested about USD 28 billion in India.
Core Nordic countries: Denmark, Finland, Iceland (least populous), Norway and Sweden (most populous).
India and Sweden elevated ties to a Strategic Partnership and adopted the India-Sweden Joint Action Plan 2026-2030.
India and Sweden launched LeadIT at the UN Climate Action Summit in 2019 and endorsed joint development of SITAC, the India-Sweden Technology and Artificial Intelligence Corridor.

subtopics.title: Italy and Netherlands: Partnerships and Heritage
subtopics.summary: India and Italy upgraded ties to a Special Strategic Partnership, targeting EUR 20 billion in bilateral trade by 2029 and backing the IMEEC corridor. Cooperation with the Netherlands covers semiconductors, water management and the return of 11th-century Chola copper plates. The booklet also places the Afsluitdijk Dam in the Netherlands alongside the proposed Kalpasar Project in Gujarat.
facts: India and Italy upgraded bilateral relations to a Special Strategic Partnership.
India and Italy committed to raising bilateral trade to EUR 20 billion by 2029.
Both nations support IMEEC, which aims to improve trade connectivity, logistics, energy and digital links between Asia and Europe.
2027 is declared the Year of Culture and Tourism between India and Italy, marking 80 years of diplomatic relations.
Italy is India's 4th largest trading partner in the EU.
MoU between Tata Electronics and ASML supports India's semiconductor plant in Dholera, Gujarat.
Leiden University returned 11th-century Chola copper plates (Anaimangalam Copper Plates) to India.
Afsluitdijk Dam: a 32 km long barrier dam in the Netherlands that transformed the saline Zuiderzee inlet into freshwater IJsselmeer Lake.
Kalpasar Project (Gujarat): proposed dam across the Gulf of Khambhat, expected to create the world's largest freshwater reservoir.
Kalpasar objectives: freshwater storage, flood control, climate resilience, irrigation support and regional development.

quizzes.passage:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to the United Arab Emirates focused on energy security, defence, technology and investment. Energy was a central theme, with an Indian strategic reserves company signing a memorandum of understanding with Abu Dhabi National Oil Company for strategic collaboration. Talks also covered storing crude oil at Fujairah under India's Overseas Strategic Reserve Framework. Separately, Indian Oil Corporation and ADNOC signed a strategic collaboration agreement on LPG supply security, and a long-term LPG sale agreement was under consideration.

On defence and maritime matters, the framework for a Strategic Defence Partnership was advanced. A memorandum between Cochin Shipyard and Drydocks World aims to establish a ship repair cluster at Vadinar. Cooperation also includes offshore fabrication under the Maritime Development Fund Scheme.

In technology, a term sheet was signed for setting up supercomputing clusters, linked to India's AI Mission and a partnership between C-DAC and G42. Investment was also on the agenda, as two institutions agreed to explore investments in India's infrastructure sector.

Taken together, these outcomes show how India's partnership with the UAE now extends well beyond trade into petroleum security, shipbuilding, artificial intelligence and infrastructure finance. Several arrangements were signed, while others remain at the stage of proposals or discussions.

quizzes.passage:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's engagements in the Nordic region combined a visit to Norway with participation in a regional summit series. The Nordic countries form a group in Northern Europe, and India has held a series of summits with them. Relations with Norway moved to a higher level, with a focus on clean energy, climate resilience, the blue economy and green shipping. Norway also joined an Indo-Pacific initiative led by India.

Sweden was the other key partner in this round. The two countries moved their ties to a strategic partnership and adopted a joint action plan that covers the years ahead. They endorsed joint development of a technology and artificial intelligence corridor, and agreed to set up a platform for small enterprises and start-ups. Modi also received a Swedish order that is among the highest honours a head of government can receive.

Economic links also matter. Norway's sovereign wealth fund has invested in India, and a trade agreement between India and the European Free Trade Association has been signed. Together, these steps show how the Nordic engagement joins climate, technology, trade and diplomacy in one strategy. The agreements cover both existing commitments and plans for future cooperation, so the outcomes are best read as a set of linked steps rather than isolated events.
